questions.knowledge_point: Identifying a Row Operation Given the Connection Between Two Determinants
questions.problem:
Given that $det(A)=det(B),$ which of the following elementary row operations transforms matrix $A$ to matrix $B,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $det(A)=det(B)$, the row operation applied to $A$ must be to add or subtract a multiple of one row to another row. In other words, it is of the form 

$$
{R}_{j}:={R}_{j}+(k){R}_{i},\,i\ne j.
$$

By considering the given row operations that are of the above form, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}| & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =det(B).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant After Multiplying a Matrix by a Scalar
questions.problem: Suppose $X$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $det(X)=10.$ What is the value of $det(6X)?$
questions.worked_solution:
Multiplying a $n\times n$ matrix by a scalar $k$ is equivalent to multiplying each row by $k,$ and this occurs $n$ times. This leads to the result

$$
\begin{aligned}det(k\cdot X)={k}^{n}\cdot det(X).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have $k=6$ and $n=3.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}det(6X) & ={6}^{3}\cdot det(X) \\  & =216\cdot 10 \\  & =2160.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant After Multiplying a Matrix by a Scalar
questions.problem: Suppose $C$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and $det(C)=-2.$ What is the value of $det(-3C)?$
questions.worked_solution:
Multiplying a $n\times n$ matrix by a scalar $k$ is equivalent to multiplying each row by $k,$ and this occurs $n$ times. This leads to the result

$$
\begin{aligned}det(k\cdot C)={k}^{n}\cdot det(C).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have $k=-3$ and $n=4.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}det(-3C) & =(-3)^{4}\cdot det(C) \\  & =81\cdot (-2) \\  & =-162.\end{aligned}
$$

provenance.kp_title: Calculating a Determinant After Multiplying a Matrix by a Scalar

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant After Applying Several Elementary Operations
questions.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and $det(A)=23.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operations ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}$ and ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+5{R}_{3}.$ What is the value of $det(B)?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's figure out what each operation does to the determinant.

- The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}$ involves swapping two rows, so it changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.

- The operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+5{R}_{3}$ involves adding a multiple of one row to another row,  so it does not change the determinant.

Therefore, we only have to change the sign of the determinant to the opposite one. Consequently, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =-det(A) \\  & =-(23) \\  & =-23.\end{aligned}
$$

provenance.kp_title: Calculating a Determinant After Applying Several Elementary Operations

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying a Row Operation Given the Connection Between Two Determinants
questions.problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Given that $X$ and $Y$ are row equivalent matrices and $det(X)=14$, find $det(Y).$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}],\,Y=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 5 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $Y$ can be obtained from $X$ by swapping the $2$nd and the $3$rd rows. 

This changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.
Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Y) & =-det(X) \\  & =-(14) \\  & =-14.\end{aligned}
$$
